subject: Pilot SLO amendment and commercial terms for Orchid Therapeutics
messages:
From: Samantha Wu <samantha.wu@orchidtx.com>
To: david.kim@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@orchidtx.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot ask — temporary SLO adjustment for hybrid POC

Hi David,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Orchid is excited to start a hybrid cloud proof-of-concept next month. Before we begin, procurement asked if Redwood can make a small, time-limited SLO adjustment for the pilot. Our current on-prem side will route through a congested egress lane for the first 60–90 days, so we need to accept slightly lower availability during the test.

Specifically we are requesting:
- Temporary uptime SLO of 98.0% (vs your standard 99.9%) for a 90-day pilot period
- A capped remedy (service credit) if the adjusted SLO is missed — ideally a capped percentage or dollar limit so we can budget
- A pilot discount for the first month (we discussed ~20%) to offset integration effort

Attached is our SOW and a short pilot timeline. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accommodate this as a limited addendum (not a change to the MCA)? If so, we’ll connect legal and procurement to finalize.

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Wu
Head of Integrations, Orchid Therapeutics
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Wu <samantha.wu@orchidtx.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot ask — temporary SLO adjustment for hybrid POC

Hi Samantha — appreciate the clear ask and the SOW.

We can accommodate a limited pilot exception with the right guardrails. High-level proposal from our side:
- Pilot SLO: 98.0% uptime for a fixed 90-day pilot window
- Remedy: service credit calculated pro rata but capped at 2% of monthly invoice or $50k (whichever is lower) per month
- Commercial: one-time 20% discount for month 1; month 2–3 at 10% (if the customer prefers larger up-front discount we can discuss)
- Documentation: addendum to be scoped as a pilot amendment with explicit sunset and telemetry checkpoints; no change to the master SLA

I’m attaching a short SLO amendment draft for your legal team to review. I’ll loop in our deal lead Marissa and legal (Jonas) to run internal approval.

If Orchid can confirm cadence of telemetry and what constitutes recovery (full failovers vs degraded responses), that will help us lock the remedy formula.

Best,
David
David Kim
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: dealdesk@redwoodinference.com, jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com, sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com
Cc: david.kim@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pilot ask — temporary SLO adjustment for hybrid POC (Orchid) — request for executive clearance

Team, forwarding Orchid’s request and David’s proposal. Quick context: Orchid is a mid-stage biotech doing a hybrid POC that could convert to a multi-region contract if pilot succeeds. The commercial ask is modest but the SLO deviation would be non-standard.

Requested approval items:
- Approve pilot exception: SLO 98.0% for 90 days
- Approve remedy cap: 2% of monthly invoice or $50k cap (whichever is lower)
- Approve pilot pricing: 25% off month 1, 10% off months 2–3 (we can move to 20% / 10% if preferred)

Please see attached pricing model and risk calc. Jonas — can you confirm redline language for the addendum? Sean — need one-off exec clearance here to avoid slowing the procurement cycle.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Deal Desk & Enterprise GTM, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, david.kim@redwoodinference.com, sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot ask — temporary SLO adjustment for hybrid POC (Orchid) — request for executive clearance

Thanks — a few legal points before we sign off:
1) Precedent: we should make the addendum explicit that it is a time-limited pilot exception and does not amend the Master Customer Agreement or the global SLA.
2) Sunset & telemetry: include a 90-day sunset plus a clause allowing either party to terminate the pilot earlier if telemetry indicates unacceptable risk. Define "downtime" measurement method (region-level vs service-level).
3) Credit mechanics: cap is fine but we should add a monthly aggregate cap across all remedies for Orchid so exposure is predictable.
4) Audit & logs: require Orchid to enable our telemetry hooks (basic traces/latency histograms) during the pilot and provide a weekly sync.

Also need finance to sign off on the revenue impact and an explicit line in the addendum that this is not a pricing precedent.

I drafted redline comments in the attached SLO_Amendment_Draft.docx. Once Dave/Marissa confirm numbers, I can convert to an executable addendum.

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com, finance@redwoodinference.com
Cc: samantha.wu@orchidtx.com
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot ask — financial impact and guardrails

Finance and team — attaching a simple model (pilot_pricing_model.xlsx) with the expected revenue and worst-case exposure assuming the SLO is missed each month. Top-level numbers:
- Expected pilot ARR (annualized): $1.2M if converted
- One-time discount cost (month 1 at 25%): ~$15k revenue reduction
- Worst-case monthly credit exposure under proposed cap: $50k (cap) but expected credits are likely << $5k based on projected usage distribution

Proposed operational guardrails:
- Guard the addendum with weekly telemetry checks and a recovery definition fallback;
- Add a mid-pilot review at day 45 to decide whether pilot proceeds to completion;
- Require Orchid to register their on-prem egress config so we can tune routing during the test.

If legal confirms the addendum language is restricted and finance is comfortable with the exposure, we recommend exec sign-off so procurement can finish the PO.

Thanks,
David
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, david.kim@redwoodinference.com, jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Cc: finance@redwoodinference.com, samantha.wu@orchidtx.com
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot ask — final exec decision

Team — thanks for the clear write-ups. I’m approving a limited, documented exception on the following conditions: 

1) Authorization: Approve a 90-day pilot SLO set to 98.0% uptime only for the scope defined in the attached SOW and addendum. This exception is one-off and does not change any company-wide SLA.
2) Remedy: Approve service credit as proposed — prorated credit with a monthly cap of 2% of the invoice or $50k, whichever is lower. Add a statement that cumulative credits across remedies for the month are included in the cap.
3) Commercial: Approve 25% discount for month 1, then 10% discount for months 2–3. After the pilot period pricing returns to standard list.
4) Legal & controls: Jonas to finalize addendum with sunset, telemetry requirements, and non-precedent language. Finance to confirm the credit cap is shown in the deal economics and the PO.

I want a mid-pilot review at day 45 (Marissa to schedule) and a recorded sign-off that this is limited to the named deal (DEAL-4092). Once the addendum is signed we can proceed.

Regards,
Sean Gallagher
Chief Commercial Officer, Redwood Inference
